name: payer-agents-egress
notes: Single source of truth for two enforcement points: the local GuardedTransport simulator and the Azure Cognitive Services Responsible AI policy deployed by infra/modules/rai-egress-policy.bicep.
Roll out in Audit first. Switch mode to Enforced only after the Application Insights 'Network egress decision' records show no unexpected would-deny entries.
Foundry platform domains are allow-listed by the service itself; a Deny default does not sever the runtime's own connectivity.
PREVIEW: network egress controls for Foundry hosted agents are in public preview, carry no preview SLA, and Microsoft states they are not intended for production.

rules.name: allow-fhir-via-apim
rules.description: The governed MCP and FHIR surface. The only clinical data path the agent is permitted to use.

rules.name: allow-search
rules.description: Azure AI Search for plan benefits and medical policy retrieval.

rules.name: allow-foundry-inference
rules.description: Foundry model inference, including the decision deployment.

rules.name: allow-cognitive-services
rules.description: Content safety and language services inside the compliance boundary.

rules.name: deny-raw-fhir-backend
rules.description: Clinical data must traverse API Management so the call is authenticated, rate limited and audited. Direct backend access bypasses all three.

rules.name: deny-public-model-apis
rules.description: No PHI to a processor outside the agreement set.

rules.name: deny-paste-sites
rules.description: Named exfiltration destination. Redundant under a Deny default, and kept because an explicit rule produces a named audit record instead of an anonymous default-deny.
